Farmers | Congresswoman Teresa Leger Fernández <div> <div> </div> </div> </div> <div> <p dir="ltr">Our ranchers and farmers are an important part of New Mexican culture and the American economy. They are key voices at the table as we think of the future of our country. That’s why I spent several months on a Farm to Congress tour to meet with farmers, ranchers, nutrition experts, and others across my district. I bring these stories of my district’s farmers with me to DC.</p> <p dir="ltr">In Congress, I have fought hard to bring justice to dairy farmers whose cattle were contaminated by toxic chemicals from Cannon Air Force Base. I secured compensation for these farmers, and I am pushing Cannon to clean up the PFAS contamination. I also secured an amendment to the PFAS Action Act to make sure that the EPA considers the dangers of these chemicals on water used for agriculture.</p> <p dir="ltr">Every five years, Congress must pass a new Farm Bill to make improvements and changes to federal agriculture, nutrition, conservation, and forestry programs. The Farm Bill is one of our best opportunities to make sure that our local communities receive the support they deserve. Below are some of my priorities for the Farm Bill that I crafted after conversations with New Mexicans.</p> <p dir="ltr">From appropriately-designed machinery to child care development in rural areas, I want to address the consistent and unique concerns that I heard from women farmers and ranchers.</p> <p dir="ltr">My bill, the Women in Agriculture Act, would help women in agriculture access the resources, equipment, and assistance they need.&nbsp;</p> <p dir="ltr">From Aztec to Roswell, farmers and ranchers across New Mexico know that agua es vida. Yet, they sometimes lack the proper resources for water conservation. That’s why I introduced the Support the WEST Act. This bill would enhance programs that support drought-resilient agriculture and water-conserving practices. Our Planet | Congresswoman Teresa Leger Fernández <div> <div> </div> </div> </div> <div> <p dir="ltr">We know that when we take care of the land that we call home, it takes care of us. As a member of the House Committee on Natural Resources, I work tirelessly to take care of the spaces we share so that generations after us can keep breathing clean air and drinking clean water.&nbsp;</p> <p dir="ltr">In New Mexico, we know that agua es vida. Since I arrived in Congress, I have helped secure over $778 million for water projects across my district including the Navajo-Gallup Water Supply Project and the Ute Water Pipeline. The Bipartisan Infrastructure Law, which I helped pass, provided the single-largest investment of water infrastructure in history. That will help small towns and villages throughout New Mexico access clean and reliable water.&nbsp;&nbsp;</p> <p dir="ltr">I also introduced the Orphaned Wells Cleanup and Jobs Act of 2021 to clean up over 56,000 known “orphaned” oil and gas wells across the country that leak methane, contaminate groundwater, and threaten the safety of communities. The infrastructure funding in the Bipartisan Infrastructure Law incorporated aspects of my bill and made $560 million available in funding to clean up orphaned wells and create jobs for New Mexico and other states.&nbsp;</p> <p dir="ltr">Climate change poses an existential threat to our planet and our ways of life. That’s why I proudly voted for the Inflation Reduction Act (IRA), which President Biden signed into law on August 16, 2022. The IRA is the largest action to combat the climate crisis in our nation’s history. It invests in clean energy production and manufacturing right here in the United States and puts us on track to reduce carbon emissions by 40 percent by 2030. That means new good-paying jobs and energy security for New Mexicans. With smart investments and strategic use of our vast renewable energy resources, New Mexico is uniquely positioned to become a leader in clean energy, growing our economy and creating good-paying jobs.</p> </div>" /> Skip to Co

Broadband | Congresswoman Teresa Leger Fernández <div> <div> </div> </div> </div> <div> <p dir="ltr">As a co-chair of the Rural Broadband Caucus, I’ll continue to advocate for policies that connect New Mexicans to the internet and each other. Broadband is basic infrastructure. It’s as necessary now as electricity once was. Internet connections can help doctors consult on patient care, expand education, and open job opportunities.&nbsp;</p> <p dir="ltr">That is why I voted for the American Rescue Plan at the height of the pandemic. It provided $7.1 billion to reimburse schools and libraries – central points for connectivity in many communities – to purchase equipment such as hotspots, internet service, and computers on behalf of students and patrons, which are essential for homework, hybrid and remote learning. I also voted for the Bipartisan<a href="https://fernandez.house.gov/dpcc-infrastructure-investment-and-jobs-act-funding-guide"><u>&nbsp;Infrastructure Law</u></a>, the largest broadband investment in our nation’s history.</p> <p dir="ltr">The Bipartisan Infrastructure Law included $65 billion for broadband so every American has access to reliable broadband, especially rural and low-income families. This funding helped more than 184,000 households afford their monthly internet bill through the Affordable Connectivity Program. Additionally, it allocated $675 million to New Mexico from the Broadband Equity Access and Deployment (BEAD) Program to help get high-speed internet coverage across the state and&nbsp; billions of dollars more to improve broadband connectivity for Tribal and rural areas.&nbsp;</p> </div>" /> Skip to Content Broadband Share on Facebook Share on Twitter Print this Page Share by Email As a co-chair of the Rural Broadband Caucus, I’ll continue to advocate for policies that connect New Mexicans to the internet and each other. Democracy | Congresswoman Teresa Leger Fernández Growing up, democracy was a deeply held value in my home. I often tell the story of my grandmother, who when she was literally in hospice, she’d call up people in Spanish and say, "you need to make sure you get to vote." Voting has always been what defines us as a democracy. Voting should be a celebration. It’s an opportunity to use your voice. That’s why I am committed to protecting this right for every American.&nbsp;</p> <p dir="ltr">During my time in Congress, I have fought for laws that safeguard this simple—yet sacred– pillar of our democracy. That’s why I voted for the&nbsp;<a href="https://fernandez.house.gov/media/press-releases/rep-leger-fernandez-stands-voting-rights-legislation"><u>Freedom to Vote: John R. Lewis Act</u></a>&nbsp;to make sure that Native Americans, Latinos, African Americans, and every other American has access to the ballot. This bill would protect poll workers, reinstate preclearance, and remove barriers to voting for those living on tribal lands. Finally, this bill would reform our campaign finance system to make sure that our democracy works for the people and not special interests.&nbsp;</p> <p dir="ltr">To protect our democracy I also voted for the&nbsp;<a href="https://fernandez.house.gov/media/press-releases/rep-leger-fernandez-votes-historic-bipartisan-presidential-election-reform-act"><u>Presidential Election Reform Act</u></a>&nbsp;to make sure that the candidate who wins the election takes office. I cosponsored the&nbsp;<a href="https://fernandez.house.gov/media/press-releases/rep-leger-fernandez-statement-january-6th-anniversary"><u>Protecting Our Democracy Act</u></a>&nbsp;to prevent foreign influence in our elections. I will always fight to make sure political violence, threats, intimidation, and lies don’t undermine over two hundred years of democratic tradition in this country.</p> <p dir="ltr">Our democracy requires justice for all including equal treatment under the law. Economic Prosperity | Congresswoman Teresa Leger Fernández <div> <div> </div> </div> </div> <div> <p dir="ltr">I am working hard to lower costs and create opportunities for economic prosperity across New Mexico. That means investing in families and workers, making housing more affordable, and spurring economic development.&nbsp;</p> <p dir="ltr"><u>Lifting Children Out of Poverty</u></p> <p dir="ltr">With nearly 1 in 4 of New Mexico’s children living in poverty, our state has one of the highest child poverty rates in the nation. We must fix that. I voted for the American Rescue Plan Act, which expanded the Child Tax Credit to create economic opportunities for families. In my district alone, this life-saving investment delivered $207.9 million to more than 78,000 families. I am disappointed that the expanded CTC expired at the end of 2021. I will always stand for the children of New Mexico and do anything in my power to help them. Please be assured that I will not give up on the expanded CTC.&nbsp;</p> <p dir="ltr"><u>Fighting for Workers</u></p> <p dir="ltr">Workers are the backbone of our economy. They deserve fair treatment and a voice in the workplace. I cosponsored the <a href="https://www.congress.gov/bill/118th-congress/house-bill/20">PRO Act</a> to protect workers from anti-union intimidation and make sure they can hold free and fair union elections. I also support the Raise the Wage Act to make sure wages keep up with rising costs of living.&nbsp;</p> <p dir="ltr"><u>Making Homeownership Affordable</u></p> <p dir="ltr">As housing costs soar, too many New Mexicans struggle to pay rent or achieve their dreams of homeownership. I believe all of our neighbors deserve to afford to live in the communities they grew up in. That’s why I introduced my&nbsp;<a href="https://fernandez.house.gov/hoyo">Home of Your Own Act</a>, which would create a new homeownership assistance program that would provide one-time, $30,000 grants to eligible first-time homebuyers nationwid

Education | Congresswoman Teresa Leger Fernández <div> <div> </div> </div> </div> <div> <p dir="ltr">Education sets the foundation for our children who will become the next generation of leaders. We must make sure they have all of the necessary tools to be successful.&nbsp;</p> <p dir="ltr">As a Member of the Education and Workforce Committee, I am working hard to support students at every age. I began my lifelong love of learning as a Head Start baby and launched the bipartisan&nbsp;<a href="https://fernandez.house.gov/media/press-releases/bipartisan-group-members-launch-bicameral-head-start-congress-caucus#:~:text=WASHINGTON%2C%20D.C.%20%E2%80%93%20June%2018%2C,to%20Congress%20Caucus%20last%20Thursday."><u>Head Start to Congress Caucus</u></a>&nbsp;because I know the opportunities that early childhood education creates. To improve elementary and secondary schools, we need to invest in teachers and make sure schools have adequate resources. My&nbsp;<a href="https://fernandez.house.gov/media/press-releases/leger-fernandez-lujan-hayes-reintroduce-legislation-expand-federal-loan"><u>Loan Forgiveness for Educators Act</u></a>&nbsp;would help teachers pay back student loans. I also cosponsored the&nbsp;<a href="https://www.congress.gov/bill/118th-congress/house-bill/1591" target="_blank" rel="noopener nofollow noreferrer" title="(opens in a new window)"><u>Advancing Toward Impact Aid Full Funding&nbsp;Act</u></a>&nbsp;to increase funding for many public schools in New Mexico.&nbsp;</p> <p dir="ltr">I also want to make sure higher education is available to all students. My&nbsp;<a href="https://fernandez.house.gov/media/press-releases/leger-fernandez-baldwin-scott-dean-introduce-legislation-lower-cost-community"><u>America’s College Promise Act</u></a>&nbsp;would support tuition-free community college and invest in Hispanic Serving Institutions and Tribal Colleges and Universities. Gender Equity | Congresswoman Teresa Leger Fernández <div> <div> </div> </div> </div> <div> <p dir="ltr">As the first Latina to serve New Mexico’s third district, I recognize and celebrate the women, like Nina Otero Warren, upon whose shoulders we stand and the girls whose bright futures lie ahead.</p> <p dir="ltr">I trust women to make decisions about their bodies. The Supreme Court’s decision to overturn Roe v. Wade not only stripped away a woman's right to choose but ripped away our right to privacy in our bedrooms, marriages, and doctor’s offices. That’s why I cosponsored the&nbsp;<a href="https://www.congress.gov/bill/118th-congress/house-bill/12" target="_blank" rel="noopener nofollow noreferrer" title="(opens in a new window)"><u>Women’s Health Protection&nbsp;Act</u></a>&nbsp;(WHPA) so all women, regardless of zip code, have the freedom to make their own health care decisions. In addition, I cosponsored the&nbsp;<a href="https://www.congress.gov/bill/118th-congress/house-bill/4121" target="_blank" rel="noopener nofollow noreferrer" title="(opens in a new window)"><u>Right to Contraception&nbsp;Act</u></a>&nbsp;and&nbsp;<a href="https://www.congress.gov/bill/118th-congress/house-bill/7056" target="_blank" rel="noopener nofollow noreferrer" title="(opens in a new window)"><u>Access to Family Building Act</u>&nbsp;</a>so women can access birth control options and IVF.&nbsp;</p> <p dir="ltr">As Vice Chair of the Democratic Women’s Caucus, I am also working to make sure that we provide economic security for women. I cosponsored the&nbsp;<a href="https://www.congress.gov/bill/118th-congress/house-bill/5433" target="_blank" rel="noopener nofollow noreferrer" title="(opens in a new window)"><u>Child Care Stabilization&nbsp;Act</u></a>&nbsp;to make sure child care providers continue to receive a reliable source of funding to help them deli

Health | Congresswoman Teresa Leger Fernández <div> <div> </div> </div> </div> <div> <p dir="ltr">As a breast cancer survivor, I know that all Americans have a right to quality, affordable health care in the communities they call home.&nbsp;&nbsp;</p> <p dir="ltr">In all corners of New Mexico, I hear tragic stories about doctor and nurse shortages and rural hospital closures. It is all too common to travel for hours to receive care. We must make bold investments to recruit and maintain a strong health care workforce. That is why I have cosponsored bills like the&nbsp;<a href="https://www.congress.gov/bill/118th-congress/house-bill/834" target="_blank" rel="noopener nofollow noreferrer" title="(opens in a new window)"><u>Rural Physician Workforce Production&nbsp;Act&nbsp;</u></a>and&nbsp;<a href="https://www.congress.gov/bill/118th-congress/house-bill/6205" target="_blank" rel="noopener nofollow noreferrer" title="(opens in a new window)"><u>Healthcare Workforce Resilience&nbsp;Act</u></a>&nbsp;that would improve our chronic rural healthcare workforce shortages by recruiting and retaining doctors in rural areas.&nbsp;</p> <p dir="ltr">We must also lower the cost of health care. I strongly support fully funding and strengthening Medicare, Medicaid, and our nation’s network of community health centers to make sure everyone can access care. I proudly voted for the&nbsp;<a href="https://drive.google.com/file/d/1LeKkyHEkDYlhD6lGhNQCJXg_Wlvwx3qi/view" target="_blank" rel="noopener nofollow noreferrer" title="(opens in a new window)"><u>Inflation Reduction&nbsp;Act&nbsp;</u></a>(IRA), which President Biden signed into law on August 16, 2022. This landmark law lowers health care premiums and allows Medicare to negotiate drug prices and cap out-of-pocket costs at $2,000.&nbsp;</p> <p dir="ltr">Like my own family, too many New Mexicans know the pain of losing a loved one to addiction.
